newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm as U.S. gasoline holds gains.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm as U.S. gasoline holds gains.

text.p: IPE Brent ended firmer on Tuesday, drawing strength from a bounding U.S. market which lurched higher again amid expectations that weekly stocks data will reveal a tightening supply situation.

September Brent closed 18 cents higher at $18.59 a barrel, failing to match the pace of August unleaded gasoline futures which closed 1.5 cents a gallon higher ahead of the contract expiry on Thursday.
Earlier, August gas oil ended 75 cents up at $167.75 a tonne, having failed to breach resistance at $168.
"Everything is following the gasoline, but crude just hasn't got the same strength to the upside that we're seeing on gasoline," said one broker.
The U.S. gasoline market has been buoyed recently by tight supplies of methyl tertiary butane ether (MTBE).
MTBE is a key blending component used in converting conventional unleaded to reformulated gasoline, the grade deliverable against the NYMEX contract.

News that Exxon Corp had shut its 110,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at its 411,000 bpd Baytown, Texas refinery after a lightening strike encouraged more short-covering on gasoline, brokers said.
"No-one wants to be short ahead of the APIs," another broker said.

Traders were expecting weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), due after the close of trade, to show a draw on gasoline stocks of up to two million barrels as high seasonal demand outstrips production.
Crude stocks are expected to fall one to three million barrels while distillate stocks are seen rising one to two million barrels.

Oil traders were still awaiting news about the timing of Iraqi exports. A United Nations spokesman said on Tuesday that Iraq's aid plan under the "oil-for-food" deal can be completed by the end of the week.
This would clear the way for approval of the plan by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan which in turn would allow moves towards resuming exports to begin.
Although Iraq has not exported oil under the current 90 day sales period which began on June 8, the U.N. late last week ruled out moving the start date forward.
As a result, Iraq would have to sell up to $1 billion worth of crude by September 5 or forfeit some sales.
